description: Frozen responses from the live sources, for parser tests that run offline. See README.md.

fixtures.describes: Lög um vexti og verðtryggingu nr. 38/2001 — 'vaxtalög'. Nine chapters, fifteen temporary provisions numbered in roman, one repealed article. The act whose short name is nowhere in its own title, which is what Act.aliases exists for.

Jarðalög nr. 81/2004. Lettered articles inserted by amendment (7. gr. a–d, 10. gr. a), per-article headings, an annex, five repealed articles. The lettered articles are the shape that lib/legal-citations.ts silently failed to extract before 2026-08-31.

The GDPR, consolidated version — the 'consolidated' layout, which is the in-force text of every amended EU act. Eleven chapters, fifteen sections nested inside them, 99 articles, and paragraph numbers printed in a span of their own, which is the part a naive parse splits from the sentence it numbers.

Decision (EU) 2016/245 of the European Central Bank — the 'oj' layout, everything published in the Official Journal since about 2004. Chapters with sections, 41 articles, two annexes, tables, and a citation number (2016/245) that is not the number in its CELEX (32016D0002).

The e-Commerce Directive 2000/31/EC — the 'legacy' layout, which Cellar holds as plain HTML with no structure at all: article headings are bare paragraphs, and the recitals above them cite Articles 251, 95 and 46 of the Treaty, which is what the adoption-formula boundary exists to keep out.

Reglugerð nr. 300/2020 um Vatnajökulsþjóðgarð, from the API with its consolidated text. Seven chapters, 44 articles, three amending regulations folded in, and the closing 'sett er samkvæmt … laga nr. 60/2007' that the lagastoð link will be built from. The structured markup generation.

Byggingarreglugerð nr. 112/2012 — the awkward one, and the reason two parser bugs were caught before release. 439 articles numbered hierarchically ('1.2.1. gr.', which is not article 1), nested HLUTI/KAFLI divisions, and a definitions article whose body is an
    of 726
  1. with no

    at all.
An amending regulation. Never stored as a row of its own; its effects[] names the base regulation it changes, which is the whole of this adapter's change detection.

A page whose regulation the API serves as a stub, but which carries the structured markup anyway — which is why the parser decides the generation by looking at the markup rather than by where the bytes came from or how old the regulation is.

The Word-converted generation, which is about three quarters of the register: no classes, no anchors, an article being a centred paragraph reading '4. gr.' and its heading the centred italic line above. What Act.structureSource exists to flag.
One page of the register: 30 of 14,648 entries across 489 pages, each flagged base or amending. More than half the register is amending.

fixtures.via: https://web.archive.org/web/2021/… — /altext/ is served through Cloudflare and refuses requests from this development environment, while /lagas/ from the same machine answers. The Wayback toolbar block was removed; nothing else was touched.
fixtures.describes: Frumvarp til jarðalaga — þskj. 1194 of the 130th þing, the bill that became lög nr. 81/2004. A whole one: the bill's articles, a 36,000-character greinargerð, and seventy-five articles commented on one by one, including a two-article heading ('Um 5. og 6. gr.') and three temporary provisions that name no article at all. The page also lists the case's other six documents, which is this app's only route to a bill's nefndarálit.

Fjárlagafrumvarp 2023 — the failure mode. The newer header form ('Þingskjal 1 — 1. mál.' rather than 'Þskj. 1194 — 783. mál.'), a title line that gives the document's category before its name, and no document at all: the text is a 368-page PDF beside the page, leaving several thousand characters of site navigation that a parser must not mistake for a bill.
